candidate.answerReason: Multiplying powers with the same base adds their exponents: 2000^1 times 2000^2000 equals 2000^2001.

methods.label: Add the exponents
methods.explanation:
The factor \(2000^{2000}\) is a product of \(2000\) copies of \(2000\). Multiplying by one more copy gives \(2001\) copies. Equivalently, the same-base exponent rule gives
\[
2000(2000^{2000})
=2000^1\cdot2000^{2000}
=2000^{2001}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{2000^{2001}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: This is a direct application of the elementary rule for multiplying powers with the same base.
